what: Banco de Chile is one of Chile's largest banks, founded in 1893 and part-owned by Citigroup and the Luksic family. It does retail, commercial and corporate banking across the country.
customers: Chilean households, small businesses and large corporations.
money: deposits, mortgages, consumer loans and cards
moat: One of the strongest deposit franchises in a concentrated Chilean banking market, with a conservative lending record through several commodity cycles.
risks: Chilean economic growth depends heavily on copper prices
Chilean inflation-linked assets mean results swing with inflation
Political debate over pension and banking reform creates uncertainty
opportunities: Net margin of 40%, among the highest of any listed bank
Chilean interest rates have stabilised, supporting lending margins
watch: Net interest margin and the non-performing loan ratio.
